function.name: cmd_controller_execute
function.description: Executes a system-level command using os.system() on Windows operating systems. It can execute single or multiple commands chained with '&&'. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

command.description: The system command to be executed. To execute multiple commands, separate them with '&&'. For example, 'dir && echo done'.

unit.description: Specifies the unit of measure for the command if applicable. This is not utilized by os.system() directly but can be used for logging or analysis purposes.

message.content:
I don’t actually “see” what’s installed on your computer, so I’ll give you a quick way to find out yourself—either from the command line or through a tiny bit of scripting.  
Below are two options depending on which shell you’re comfortable with.

---

### Option 1 – Quick one‑liner in **PowerShell**

```powershell
$path = "${env:SystemRoot}\System32\msedge.exe"; # Edge uses this name
If ((Test-Path "$Env:LOCALAPPDATA\\Microsoft\\Edge\\Application\\msedge.exe") `
    -Or (Test-Path "$Env:PROGRAMFILES\\Google\\Chrome\\ Application\\chrome.exe")) {
    Write-Host "✅ Google Chrome appears to be installed."
}
Else { 
    Write-Warning "❌ Google Chrome does NOT appear to be installed." 
}
```

*What it does:*  
Checks both common install locations (`%LocalAppData%\Google\Chrome\Application`) and `%ProgramFiles%\Google\Chrome\Application`). If either exists, it reports success.

> ⚡️ *Tip*: Run the above block inside PowerShell (right‑click → “Run as administrator”) to avoid permission issues when probing protected folders.

---

### Option 2 – Batch / CMD version

```batch
@echo off
setlocal EnableDelayedExpansion

rem Check Program Files folder first
for %%i in ("%ProgramFiles(x86)%","%ProgramFiles%") do (
   set "chk=%%~fi\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe"
   if exist "!chk!" goto found
)

rem Fallback to Local App Data
set chk=%LocalAppData%\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe
if exist "%chk%" goto found

goto notfound

:found
echo ✅ Google Chrome seems to be installed at !chk!
exit /b 0

:notfound
echo ❌ Google Chrome was not detected.
exit /b 1
```

Save the text into a `.bat` file and double‑click it—or call it from another script—to get instant feedback.

---

#### Why those paths?

| Path | Typical Install Location |
|------|--------------------------|
| `%ProgramFiles%\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe` | 64‑bit installs on most PCs |
| `%ProgramFiles(x86)%\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe` | 32‑bit installs on 64‑bit machines |
| `%LocalAppData%\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe` | Portable/“Click‑Once” installations |

These three cover almost all standard setups.  

---

### What if you’re on macOS/Linux?

On macOS you’d look under `/Applications/Google Chrome.app`, while Linux users typically install via package managers (`apt`, `dnf`, etc.) where you can simply run:

```bash
which google-chrome || which chromium-browser
```

---

**Bottom line:**  
Use whichever method feels easiest for you. Once you’ve run the appropriate check, you should see a clear “yes” or “no” output telling you whether Chrome is present on your machine.
